html:
SMTO-CFG-0105 — The website's download list has invalid version details

GUID: 4a0c0f83-1971-5c13-bd25-dab299097668
Slug: public-site-release-invalid
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: public

What happened

  • The list of SMTO versions offered for download has a mistake, such as a repeated version, a date without a time zone, or a test version marked as stable. The website shows downloads as unavailable until it's fixed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Find the download list the website uses: the file named by SMTO_SITE_RELEASE_MANIFEST_PATH, or the default list in the website's release_data folder. That is the file that failed the check.
  2. Rebuild it with SMTO's release tool in the scripts folder (the command is in Technical details) instead of editing it by hand. The tool works out file sizes and checksums and reports the exact mistake.
  3. Check each version: stable versions have no ending like -beta.1, beta and nightly versions do, and dates include a time zone, such as 2026-11-17T09:00:00Z. Test versions marked as stable, and dates without a time zone, are refused.
  4. From the SMTO folder, run python scripts/validate-smto-site-content.py, then restart the website. The website reads the download list only when it starts.

What success looks like

  • The check finishes without an error, and the website's download and version history pages list your versions.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message from the release tool and send it to the person who publishes SMTO versions. Don't delete older entries or published download files to get past this; correct the details instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Release manifest validation failed (schema_version not 1, invalid SemVer or stable/prerelease channel mismatch, published_at without a timezone, signing scheme or variant not matching the platform, duplicate version, artifact identity or URL, non-public URL, or a manifest file larger than 5,000,000 bytes), so release pages are served as unavailable.

What this means

  • Release manifest validation rejects semantic-version/channel inconsistency, timestamp format/timezone, signing/platform mismatch, duplicate release/artifact URLs or identities, unsupported version or excessive file size. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Release manifest validation rejects semantic-version/channel inconsistency, timestamp format/timezone, signing/platform mismatch, duplicate release/artifact URLs or identities, unsupported version or excessive file size.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific release/platform identity, timestamp and manifest bound before publication.

How to fix it

  • Regenerate the manifest at SMTO_SITE_RELEASE_MANIFEST_PATH (default src/smto_site/release_data/releases.json) with scripts/generate-smto-release-manifest.py, which hashes the real artifacts and validates against src/smto_site/releases.py. Then run python scripts/validate-smto-site-content.py and restart the site. The site only logs release_registry_unavailable, so use the generator to see the exact failing field.
  • Correct the release version, publication timestamp and platform artifact metadata, then validate the manifest before publishing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm current state and correct the reported condition before requesting another attempt. Do not replay work with an unknown outcome.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended manifest validates with unique consistent releases and supported artifact metadata.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained evidence or retry an operation whose effect is unknown.
